evidence: renderDslLine already calls registry.applyInput as its own step 1 (src/dsl/render.ts:321), confirmed by the agent's citation; the daemon's extra pre-apply ran the MobX action twice per render and could clobber last_error on the second pass, a real double-invocation bug, not a style nit.
guidance_note: When wrapping a function that already performs a canonical side effect as its documented first step, don't re-invoke that same effect at the call site before handing off.

evidence: The docstring claimed all provider calls ran in parallel, but blockProvider was awaited after the Promise.all batch, which is a literal code/comment mismatch and a real latency cost the agent fixed by folding it into the same batch.

metricsProvider fields could be null but the code coerced them to 0 with ?? 0, which collapses 'no data' into a fake real zero and breaks the documented missing-field-uses-DSL-default contract; making MetricsPayload's fields optional and projecting only non-null fields is a direct fix of the stated contract violation.
guidance_note: When a payload contract distinguishes 'missing' from 'zero', keep that distinction all the way from the provider return type through to the type the DSL sees -- a ?? 0 at the boundary silently erases it.

evidence: The agent's own reply concedes this is 'a real regression on my side' -- the legacy renderer gated the metrics fetch on segment presence and the rewrite dropped that gate, so metrics.getMetricsInfo (a transcript JSONL parse plus file walk) ran on every render regardless of layout.
guidance_note: When replacing a renderer that had a segment-presence gate, port the gate (even if reshaped) before shipping the new hot path -- don't let an optimization silently regress to running everything unconditionally.

evidence: Confirmed against 5170f16's actual diff (gh api repos/promptctl/cc-candybar/commits/5170f16): buildNeededPrefixes there scanned the config for any kind:input declaration, not for reachability from config.layout, so the shipped DEFAULT_DSL_CONFIG's reference-complete declarations kept every provider firing regardless of layout -- exactly the gap F5 names. The round-2 fix replaced this with a real BFS from config.layout.
guidance_note: A gate meant to reflect whether something is actually rendered must walk from the render root (layout) outward, not check whether it is declared anywhere -- a reference-complete default config will always satisfy the weaker check.

evidence: Confirmed via gh api repos/promptctl/cc-candybar/commits/5170f16 --jq .files[].filename: 5170f16 touched only render-payload.ts and server.ts, not cache/render.ts, so this dead args cache-key field predates that commit and was part of the original round-0 diff (0b8a005) -- the ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT flag is a false positive here; Copilot's review simply reached this file one round later, it was not introduced or left behind by 5170f16.

Same false-positive pattern as F6: cache/render.ts (where the unused usageProvider dep lives) was not part of 5170f16's diff (confirmed via the commit's file list), so this dead dependency was present since round 0, not caused by the named fix.

default-dsl-config.ts (where the eager kind:shell tmux declaration lives) is also absent from 5170f16's file list, confirming this subprocess-at-registration bug predates that fix and is an original round-0 gap Copilot caught in round 1, not something 5170f16 introduced.
guidance_note: A kind:shell variable declaration runs its subprocess at registration time regardless of layout membership -- anything meant to be layout-gated must be sourced as kind:input from the payload builder, not declared as a source kind that self-executes.

evidence: Verified firstPopulatedEntry already existed verbatim in round-0 commit 0b8a005 (grep found two matches there) and was untouched by 973f54c's diff, so this debug-introspection bug is an original-PR defect surfaced in round 2, not caused by the round-1 fix it's flagged against.

973f54c's diff for cache/render.ts touches only cacheKey and RenderDeps (confirmed by grepping its patch for rebindWatcher/resolvedPath, which returns nothing) -- the hot-reload-never-activates-when-no-file-exists gap predates that commit. The round-3 fix (candidate-dir watching via a single enumerator) is a real, well-scoped correctness fix regardless.

README.md is not in 973f54c's file list, so this doc bug (unbraced when expression) predates that commit; it's a genuine documentation defect (evaluateWhen only hides on the literal string false, so a bare ne .branch expression always renders) that the agent correctly traced to the templating engine's actual behavior.

ae8f9c7's diff for cache/render.ts (fetched directly) only touches rebindWatcher/refreshWatcher, not the dispose-then-register sequence in reloadInto that F12 is about -- this last-known-good-loss bug predates ae8f9c7. Build-then-swap is the correct general fix: it makes a failed reload never destroy the entry's last-good state.
guidance_note: When swapping a live resource for a newly-constructed replacement, build the replacement fully (letting any construction failure be caught) before disposing the resource being replaced -- dispose-then-build turns any construction failure into total loss of the old state.

evidence: CLAUDE.md still described the cache key as (args, projectDir, cwd) after F6's fix (973f54c) had already dropped args from cacheKey -- the doc went stale as a direct, unremediated side effect of that earlier code fix, which is the comment-drift-from-fix pattern this audit is hunting.
guidance_note: When a fix changes a cache key's or data structure's actual identity fields, grep the repo's docs (CLAUDE.md, README) for that structure's description in the same commit -- don't let the next reviewer catch the doc separately.

evidence: The buildRenderPayload docstring still said providers run when a path is merely declared, but F5's fix (973f54c) had already replaced that gating with the layout-reachable BFS closure -- the docstring simply wasn't updated in the same commit that changed the semantics it describes.

dbgState was constructed with a fresh, never-populated empty Map every request, so debug segments always reported null -- a genuine broken-by-construction debug contract; wiring an actual per-entry sink that renderDslLine populates is a direct, correct fix.

WatcherRegistry.acquire replaces onInvalidate for a shared key, so two cache entries resolving to the same config file really did silently blind the first entry to reloads -- a genuine concurrency bug for the common case of two sessions in one repo; giving every cache entry its own watcher key (including projectDir/cwd) is a direct fix.
guidance_note: A registry that shares state by key (like WatcherRegistry.acquire replacing a callback) is a footgun whenever two independent callers can compute the same key -- key on the caller's own identity unless fan-out semantics are actually wanted.

evidence: Seeding the BFS frontier from every segment-local var declaration (rather than only vars actually referenced by a template) really could mark an orphan var's input path as needed and fire its provider for no reason; removing the seeding and relying on transitive reachability through actual template refs is the correct, narrower fix.

extractTemplateRefs plus exact-match lookupDecl really did miss namespace-only refs like toJson .git, which the scope proxy (src/template-engine/scope.ts) treats as a valid read of the whole namespace -- a genuine under-gating bug that would silently populate a referenced namespace with only its declared defaults. expandRef mirroring the scope proxy's own prefix semantics is the right, single-sourced fix.
guidance_note: When writing a second implementation of what a reference resolves to (here: a static reachability analyzer mirroring a runtime scope proxy), enumerate the runtime's actual resolution rules first -- a namespace-prefix read is a real access pattern the static analyzer has to know about too.

evidence: buildNeededPrefixes recomputing the same BFS over a config that is stable for the cache entry's lifetime is a real, avoidable per-render cost; hoisting it into DslRenderState computed once at buildState time is the straightforward, correct fix.

The reviewer's two suggested shapes (opt-in debug flag, or on-demand capture) both avoid capturing on every render; the agent instead always stores the already-computed laid-out cells (cheap reference storage) and defers the expensive per-segment ANSI serialization to the rare debug-segments request itself -- a materially different, and reasoned, design that still achieves the reviewer's stated goal (normal renders pay zero extra serializer cost).
args truly is dead state on CacheEntry once excluded from the cache key (per F6's fix); removing it is a straightforward, low-risk cleanup with no residual ambiguity.

SourceRegistry was hardcoded to defaultEmptyValue as an empty string, bypassing the loader-validated config.globals.default_empty_value knob entirely -- a real config-knob-ignored bug; threading the config value through is the direct fix.

The header comment in cache/render.ts still said the cache keys on (args, projectDir, cwd) after F6's fix had already dropped args -- another instance of the same doc-drift class as F13, caught and fixed the same round.

home sourced only from HOME really does regress on Windows where HOME is commonly unset in favor of USERPROFILE; routing it through the payload builder (which already exposes HOME or USERPROFILE) rather than a per-declaration env lookup is the right, single-sited fix.

getGitInfo was really called with an empty options object, so GitService's show* fields (sha, working-tree counts, upstream, stash, repoName) silently defaulted to empty even when a layout segment referenced them -- deriving GitOptions from the same neededInputPaths closure that already gates whether the provider fires at all is the correct, uniform fix.

The prior daemon-usage-cache test suite really was deleted with no replacement, leaving cache-hit/mtime-invalidation/LRU/sweep behavior untested on a hot-path class; the agent added a focused suite covering exactly those cases.

blockProvider really did duplicate responsibility with the payload builder (nativeUtilization used, timeRemaining unused, resetsAt re-read directly from hookData) -- dropping the provider and reading straight from hookData.rate_limits.five_hour for both block and weekly removes the duplicate-computation risk entirely rather than patching around it.

RenderCache's semantics really had changed substantially (keying, build-then-swap, candidate watching, disposal) with zero remaining unit tests after the prior suite was deleted; the agent added a five-case suite covering keying, last-known-good preservation, and watcher-driven reload.

Both sub-bugs are real: the ne .project_dir .current_dir guard genuinely prevented the project-root case from ever hitting the project-relative branch, and unguarded hasPrefix genuinely mis-classifies /home/alice as under /home/al; both fixes (accept-equality, boundary-safe prefix check) directly address the described mechanisms and are pinned by new tests.

rebindWatcher really did build fs.watch targets for candidate parent directories without existence checks, which throws on a fresh install where the XDG config directory doesn't yet exist; filtering to existing directories is a direct, low-risk fix with a documented and reasonable bounded limitation.
The 1.1s real sleep was a genuine flakiness and slowness risk; utimesSync to a deterministic future timestamp removes the timing dependency outright and the agent reports the measured suite speedup.

The void sanitizeTermCols call really discarded the sanitized value while a comment implied it was in effect at the boundary -- a real misleading-comment risk for future maintainers; removing the dead call and comment (rather than storing an unused value) is the cleaner of the reviewer's two suggested remedies.

Confirmed via gh api repos/promptctl/cc-candybar/commits/6944810: the composeWithError to composeWithDiagnostics rename happened in that commit, which is new feature work (accept .json plus collision warnings) unrelated to any tracked Copilot finding's fix -- so this doc drift is real but its root cause is untracked new-scope work, not an earlier finding in this batch; caused_by is left null rather than mis-attributed.
guidance_note: Renaming a function that docs cite as the canonical example of a behavior is a drift risk every time that function is touched for unrelated reasons -- grep the docs for the old name in the same commit.

evidence: Confirmed via gh api repos/promptctl/cc-candybar/commits/deeccea: the waitFor helper (which silently returns after its deadline with no failure signal) was introduced in that same commit, i.e. in the fix that added tests to answer F28 -- the new test infrastructure itself shipped with the exact passes-green-on-a-broken-watcher flaw this audit is hunting for.
guidance_note: A polling helper written to pin async behavior (fs.watch, retries, hot-reload) must fail loudly on timeout -- a silent-return waitFor makes every test that uses it worthless as a regression guard for the thing it is supposedly pinning.

evidence: Confirmed via gh api repos/promptctl/cc-candybar/commits/ba39d69: this test's HOME-env-mutation dance was written in that same commit, after F24's fix (0c2ce9c) had already switched home from kind:env to kind:input reading the payload -- the new test carried forward a technique that was already obsolete at the moment it was written, because the author didn't re-check F24's fix before authoring it.
guidance_note: When writing a new test against a variable whose source kind another recent fix just changed, write the test against the current source (the payload), not the pattern used before that fix landed.

evidence: The daemon's verb registry genuinely has no open-url handler, so enabling the default tray segment really does produce a rejected click -- confirmed against the finding's own accurate read of src/daemon/verbs/index.ts. Dropping the segment (a third option beyond the reviewer's add-the-verb or change-the-template) is a reasonable, arguably better call: it doesn't ship a broken default while punting a genuinely separable feature (both verb and template shipping together) to a real follow-up.

Naive tilde-prefix replacement really does corrupt a named-user form like ~alice/cfg into homedir-plus-alice/cfg since there's no way to resolve another user's home directory; restricting expansion to the enumerated safe forms (bare ~, ~/..., and the Windows ~\ variant) and leaving other forms untouched (one of the reviewer's two suggested remedies) turns a silent corruption into a simple file-not-found.

DIR_TEMPLATE's POSIX-only prefix and trim logic really does fail to collapse home or render project-relative paths on Windows, where paths use backslashes; normalizing path-shaped payload fields to forward slashes at the daemon boundary (posixify) means every template gets uniform separators without per-author platform branches -- matches the reviewer's first suggested remedy.

narrative: This 38-finding, 14-round PR looks at first glance like a chain of fixes causing more fixes, but cross-checking every ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT flag against the actual commit diffs (via gh api repos/promptctl/cc-candybar/commits/<sha>) shows most flagged findings' code predates the commit they're flagged against -- Copilot's review scope widened each round (39 to 45 files reviewed) over an already-complete branch, surfacing pre-existing gaps rather than fix-introduced regressions. Two genuine incomplete-fix chains exist: F4's provider-gating fix used declared-anywhere-in-config instead of reachable-from-layout, producing F5 one round later; and F28's newly-added RenderCache tests shipped a waitFor helper that silently passed on timeout, producing F34 two rounds later. Two comment/test-drift findings (F13, F35) trace to earlier fixes (F6's cache-key change, F24's home-source change) that altered behavior without updating a doc or a later-written test to match. Technical judgment throughout was strong -- findings were root-caused and fixed with matching mechanisms, not patched over -- and even the two premise-agreed-but-different-fix responses (F20, F36) were well-reasoned departures from the reviewer's literal suggestion.
guidance_observations: Because Copilot's review depth grows with each round rather than only re-diffing the incremental commit, the ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT flag on a finding is not itself evidence the flagged commit caused it -- always check the flagged commit's actual file list before assuming causality.

The two real incomplete-fix chains (F4 to F5, F28 to F34) both happened because the initial fix implemented the narrow letter of the ask (a declaration check; a polling loop) without walking the underlying invariant (reachability; failure-must-be-loud) to its edge case.
Comment and test drift (F13, F35) recurred because a code fix changed a semantic without a corresponding grep-the-docs-and-tests step in the same commit.

evidence: Confirmed via gh pr view 33 and gh api repos/promptctl/cc-candybar/commits/efd2a87: reply 1 declined the fix outright (citing single-user-workstation as the dominant deployment and filing a follow-up), then reply 2 reversed course and shipped ensureSocketParentSafe -- a plan that did not match the eventual action, i.e. mixed, not a clean pushback or a clean accept. The shipped fix (uid, mode, and symlink check before bind) is real and correct as far as it goes, but it only prevents the daemon itself from binding into an attacker-controlled directory; it does nothing to stop the Rust client from connecting to an attacker's pre-planted rogue socket at the same predictable path, which was the reviewer's actual MITM scenario -- so the closing claim that this turns a silent MITM into a visible daemon-exit failure overstates the fix's coverage, and single-enforcer is invoked defensively to justify not closing that gap rather than to describe an architecture that actually closes it.
guidance_note: When a reviewer describes a two-sided trust boundary (a socket a client connects to and a daemon binds), a one-sided mitigation doesn't retire the finding even if it's a real improvement -- say explicitly which half of the described attack remains open, rather than characterizing the partial fix as resolving the threat.

evidence: mergeWithDefault really did collapse an explicit empty layout and an absent layout to the same fallback, silently defeating a user's attempt to suppress all default segments with no warning surfaced -- confirmed by the reviewer's citation of the exact test locking in the wrong behavior. Making the merge respect RawDslConfig's three real states (absent, empty, non-empty) is a direct, correct fix, and the pre-existing test was updated to assert the corrected semantics.

narrative: Two round-0 findings, no chains. The socket-parent-permissions finding is a real, correctly-identified threat that got a genuinely mixed response -- declined, then partially implemented after a second reply -- and the shipped daemon-side-only fix leaves the client-connect half of the described attack open despite the closing characterization that it doesn't. The layout-suppression merge bug was cleanly identified and cleanly fixed with a test update. The PR's own issue-comment handoff is a notable positive: the agent explicitly flagged that this PR shipped adjacent hardening rather than its ticket's (bzh.8) described scope, which is good process hygiene independent of the review findings themselves.
guidance_observations: A security finding that gets a decline-then-partial-fix across two replies in the same thread should be classified mixed, not accepted_fix or pushed_back, since the stated plan and the eventual action diverged.

Citing a law to justify not fully closing a gap the same PR itself introduced (moving the socket into /tmp) is a different move than citing a law to describe an existing architecture -- the former deserves more scrutiny.

evidence: rich-js 0.4.0 really does require a newer Node engines range per its lockfile metadata while this package's own engines field still allowed Node 18 -- a genuine dishonest-support-range bug; bumping the engines field to match is the direct, complete fix.

The spine comments really did still describe a StripCell array and synthesized pad/marker cells after the migration to RichText eliminated both concepts -- a real stale-comment finding, fixed by refreshing the wording to match the new types.

narrative: Small, clean migration PR: two round-0 findings, an engines-field mismatch after a dependency bump and stale spine comments after the StripCell-to-RichText migration, both correctly identified and directly fixed with no dispute. Round 1 found nothing new. No chains, no process issues.
guidance_observations: When bumping a dependency to a version with a stricter engines requirement, update this package's own engines field in the same commit rather than waiting for a reviewer to notice the risk.
